title: What’s included when you hire a private chef

body_markdown:
Booking a private chef should feel like a night off, not another project. The easiest way to get there is to know exactly what your quote covers before you pay, from the shopping to the washing up.


Here’s what comes as standard with a yhangry chef, what you can add, and the questions worth asking first.


## What comes as standard


Every yhangry quote is one all-in price for your event, with no separate fees to add up later. Here’s what that covers.


Included What it means for you


Ingredients Your chef does the shopping. Ingredients are built into the price on more than 99% of bookings


Cooking in your kitchen Your chef prepares and cooks the menu on site, with some elements prepped ahead


Serving Your chef brings each course to the table


Clean-up Your chef clears down and leaves the kitchen as they found it. Customers often tell us it was left spotless


And if you’d like more:


You can add How


Extra guests Add them after booking, through a payment link from your chef


Waiting staff Ask for table service, drinks or passed canapés in your brief


Special touches A wine suggestion, a birthday dessert, a dish you love: just ask


Every event is a little different, so treat your chef’s written proposal as the detail to agree, and check anything you’re unsure about before you pay.


## Your menu and ingredients


Start with what you love. Tell your chef what you enjoy, what you’d rather avoid and roughly what you want to spend, and they’ll shape a menu around it. If you want to swap a dish, just ask: a premium ingredient or extra preparation may change the price, so your chef will confirm before anything’s final.


Your chef buys the ingredients, so there’s no shopping list for you. If you’d like to supply something yourself, such as a special cut of meat or a bottle to pair with the main, mention it early so it fits the plan.


## Your kitchen


Some dishes are prepped before your chef arrives, and the rest is cooked and finished in your kitchen. Agree an arrival time and check your kitchen suits the menu: a tasting menu and a relaxed family-style feast need different amounts of oven, worktop and fridge space.


A quick photo of your kitchen helps more than any description. If an appliance is temperamental, say so, and your chef will plan around it.


## Serving


Your chef serves each course, so you can stay at the table with your guests. For a bigger party or a more formal evening, you can add waiting staff to pour drinks, clear plates or pass canapés round. Put it in your brief and your chef will include it in the quote.


## Plates, glasses and equipment


Your chef brings what they need to cook; tableware usually comes from your home or venue. Count your plates, glasses and cutlery, and tell your chef what you have. Holiday rentals can be light on crockery, so it’s worth checking before you arrive. If you need to hire anything, agree who arranges it and when it’s collected.


## Clean-up and leftovers


This is the part people love. Your chef clears down and leaves the kitchen as they found it, so the evening ends at the table, not at the sink. If you’re in a rental with checkout rules, share them with your chef.


If there’s food left over, ask your chef what will keep and how to store it. Many are happy to set leftovers aside for you to enjoy the next day.


## A real quote, start to finish


This summer, a group staying in a rented house in Somerset booked[Chef Alex D](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/alex-d/) for a three-course dinner. Here’s how their booking came together.


What happened


Booked Mid-June, for a dinner in early August


Price About £123 a head, all in: ingredients, cooking, serving and clean-up


Menu Canapés, then guests chose two starters from five, two mains from six, fondant potatoes and a dessert


A late change One more guest joined after booking, added at the same price per head


Final total £1,358 for 11 guests


Afterwards The group added a £100 tip for Alex


The starters ranged from seared tuna carpaccio to king prawns with nduja, and the mains from dry-aged Somerset bavette to a butternut squash gnocchi for the vegetarians. The group said Alex was attentive, his timing was spot on, and he left the place clean, with leftovers set aside for them to enjoy later.


## Six questions to ask before you pay


A good chef will be happy to answer these, and the answers make it easy to compare quotes:


Keep the agreed menu, guest numbers and arrival time in your yhangry chat so you and your chef can both refer back to them. Events booked more than 30 days ahead are secured with a deposit, with the balance taken 30 days before.

FAQ


Does a private chef quote include ingredients?


On yhangry, almost always. Ingredients were included in more than 99% of bookings over the past year, built into one total price.


Do private chefs clean up afterwards?


Yes. Your chef clears down and leaves the kitchen as they found it. If you’re staying in a rental with checkout rules, share them with your chef.


Is waiting staff included?


Yes, your chef serves each course. For larger or more formal events, you can add waiting staff for drinks, table service or canapés.


Can I add guests after booking?


Yes. Your chef sends a payment link for each extra guest, so changing your numbers is easy.


Should I tip a private chef?


That’s entirely up to you. If your chef made the evening, you can add a tip through yhangry afterwards.
